=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Draft (SPA and Disclosure Letter)

**Bottom line:** The package is strongly seller-favourable and should not be accepted as "FINAL." Known issues in the data room already total well over the proposed general cap and basket, and several items are structured so the Buyer carries them without recourse. The Seller's preamble on "market" terms and "principal-level settlement" is advocacy, not a basis for acceptance. The deal team should confirm with Wattlebridge principals whether any such settlement exists, and the Buyer should not treat these positions as agreed.

---

## 1. Framing points to reject first

- **"FINAL, not to be re-opened."** Nothing has been agreed by the Buyer in this package. Confirm internally before responding.
- **"Market" terms (10–20% caps, ~1% baskets, 12–18 month periods, buyer-knowledge qualifications).** These are the Seller's characterisation. Verify against our own precedent and current SaaS deal data before conceding anything. Even if accurate, the known data-room issues mean the generic market position is not the right test.
- **Data-room date.** Disclosure runs to 5.00pm 22 September 2026. Today is 5 November 2026. Everything after that date is undisclosed and unwarranted, so a bring-down and updated data room are needed.

---

## 2. Material issues by theme

### A. Warranty recourse (Clauses 12.1 to 12.3, 13)

| Term | Seller position | Buyer concern |
|---|---|---|
| General cap | 20% of price = AUD 4.8m | Known items alone (see Section 3) approach or exceed this. Caps should be tiered: a higher general cap, with Fundamental and tax uncapped or capped at price. |
| De minimis | AUD 25k | Ambiguous whether sub-de-minimis claims count toward the basket. Clarify, and lower the threshold or aggregate small claims. |
| Basket | AUD 250k (~1.04% of price), excess only | A true deductible means the Buyer absorbs the first AUD 250k of every claim. Push for a **tipping basket** (once exceeded, recover from the first dollar). |
| General time limit | 18 months | Too short for issues that surface late (privacy, tax, IP chain of title). Push for at least 24–36 months for general warranties. |
| Single limitation rule | Any limit applies to all claims | Reject. Fundamental, tax and fraud claims need separate, longer periods tied to statutory limitation (Limitation Act 1969 (NSW)) and ATO amendment periods, with counsel to confirm the exact periods. |

### B. Fundamental warranties (title, capacity)

The Seller proposes the same caps and time limits "for administrative simplicity." This is unacceptable. Title and capacity warranties should be:
- outside the general cap, or capped at 100% of price actually received;
- subject to a long-dated or statutory limitation period;
- outside the basket and de minimis.

### C. Exclusive remedy, non-reliance, and limitations (Clauses 9.3, 12.8, 20.5)

These apply to "all Claims of any nature." Require express carve-outs for:
- fraud and dishonesty (state this expressly, even though a non-reliance clause should not be read to exclude fraud);
- Fundamental Warranties;
- specific indemnities;
- price adjustment and completion accounts claims;
- claims under the Ironquay, Riverlark, bonus and privacy items.

### D. Buyer knowledge and disclosure (Clauses 8.3, Disclosure Letter 1.1, 1.2)

This is the most aggressive position in the draft. Together, Clause 8.3 and the general disclosure effectively:
- disclose the entire data room, the Accounts, and public registers against every warranty;
- bar claims for any matter "discoverable" from public records, which is an unlimited standard.

**Push back:**
- Delete general data-room disclosure. Disclosure should be specific, fairly disclosed against a specific warranty, and reasonably particular.
- Replace Clause 8.3 with an express **pro-sandbagging clause**: the Buyer's knowledge does not prejudice any claim. Note that the common-law position on buyer knowledge is not uniform, so the express clause matters.
- Clause 1.4 ("nothing admits liability") is acceptable as drafted, provided it does not limit the warranties themselves.

### E. Conditions precedent

**Bluefen (Clauses 3, 6.3):** Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue (~30%). Consent has not been obtained, and conditions in clause 11.3 are not addressed.
- The "reasonable endeavours" framing should be replaced with a hard **condition precedent**: consent in agreed form, all clause 11.3 conditions satisfied.
- Add a long-stop date and Buyer termination right.
- Buyer waiver of the CP must be express and written, with no implied waiver on Completion.
- Consider a price adjustment if the consent is obtained with commercial conditions.

**Riverlark (Clauses 2, 7):** ~AUD 3.2m outstanding, discharge deferred to "following Completion."
- On a debt-free basis, the facility must be **repaid at Completion from Seller proceeds**, with a payoff letter and PPSR discharge delivered at Completion.
- Deferring the release leaves the Company exposed to the lender's security over its assets.
- **Verify the funds flow** actually deducts AUD 3.2m. The Seller says it "reflects the agreed price mechanics," which is not confirmation. If the debt is not deducted, the Buyer is effectively paying an extra AUD 3.2m.

**Office lease and Mossvale (Disclosure 7, 9):** Confirm whether landlord or Mossvale consent is required on a change of control. Make consent or waiver a CP where it is required, or a specific indemnity if it is not obtained.

### F. Specific items

**Employee bonuses (Disclosure 5):** AUD 420k in conditional Completion bonuses, not in the funds flow, with payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs unaddressed.
- Treat as a **debt-like item** deducted from price, or a Seller transaction cost.
- Require the on-cost calculation and a specific indemnity for any payroll tax or super liability.

**Ironquay IP (Clause 11.1, Disclosure 4):** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment (~AUD 180k open per DD-010). The problem is not the amount but the chain of title. Project Materials do not transfer until SOW3 fees are paid, and there is no receipt or confirmatory assignment in the data room.
- Make receipt of payment and an executed confirmatory assignment a **CP**.
- Add a specific, uncapped (or separately capped) IP ownership indemnity, not limited to the SOW3 payment.

**Privacy/export incident (Disclosure 6):** Up to ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps) were sent to an unintended external address. The investigation is preliminary.
- Business-contact data is still personal information under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth). The Company should assess whether the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme applies. The assessment window is limited (generally 30 days), and this matter has been open since at least September, so timeliness is a concern. Counsel should confirm the Company's obligations and whether notification has been or should be made.
- Require a forensic report before signing, a specific uncapped (or separately capped) indemnity covering investigation, notification, regulatory and third-party costs, and a privacy/data security warranty.
- The Seller's description ("preliminary," "not expected to be material") is not a substitute for evidence. Do not accept a materiality characterisation from the Seller.

**Supplier renewals (Disclosure 8):** Three renewals totalling AUD 330k, described by the Seller as "ordinary-course." The disclosure says they must be read together for timing and scope, which suggests they may be one arrangement split into three.
- Require the actual contracts, termination rights and term lengths.
- Treat unavoidable or non-terminable amounts beyond Completion as debt-like, or require an ordinary-course covenant and Buyer consent for new commitments.

**Tax and IP warranties:** The Seller treats these as "settled under the general regime." They are not. Require:
- a standalone pre-Completion tax indemnity, outside the general cap and basket;
- standalone IP warranties, including ownership, non-infringement and open-source compliance, with appropriate recourse.

**Title (Disclosure 10):** The share register at DD-012 shows Harbourglass as holder of 100%, but it is only the Seller's evidence. The Buyer should:
- run its own ASIC company extract and PPSR and dealing searches;
- require executed share transfers, confirmation of no encumbrances, and a Fundamental Warranty on title and capacity.

---

## 3. Known exposure versus proposed protection

| Item | Amount (AUD) | Current protection | Issue |
|---|---|---|---|
| Riverlark facility | ~3.2m | Release after Completion | Should be repaid from price at Completion |
| Bluefen revenue at risk | ~3.6m revenue (~30%) | Reasonable endeavours | Value impact unknown; needs CP and possibly price adjustment |
| Employee bonuses | 420k + on-costs | None (not in funds flow) | Should be debt-like |
| Supplier renewals | 330k | None | Ordinary-course characterisation unverified |
| Ironquay SOW3 | ~180k open | Indemnity limited to SOW3 | Chain of title risk beyond the payment |
| Privacy incident | Unquantified | None | Needs investigation and specific indemnity |
| General cap / basket | 4.8m / 250k | As proposed | Inadequate for known issues if these are left as warranty claims |

Items with a known amount (Riverlark, bonuses, supplier, Ironquay) should be handled through price mechanics or specific indemnities, not general warranty recourse. Warranty claims are a backstop for unknown issues. The general cap should not be the main protection against items we already know about.

---

## 4. Recommendations (summary)

1. **Reject "FINAL" status** and the principal-settlement claim until Wattlebridge confirms what, if anything, was agreed.
2. **Reject the market framing** and verify against our own precedent.
3. **Restructure the warranty package:** tiered caps, tipping basket, lower de minimis, clarified basket counting.
4. **Separate Fundamental and tax warranties:** outside general cap and basket, longer limitation periods.
5. **Carve out fraud, Fundamental, specific indemnity and price adjustment claims** from the exclusive remedy and non-reliance provisions.
6. **Delete general data-room disclosure and Clause 8.3;** insert a pro-sandbagging clause.
7. **Make Bluefen consent a hard CP** with long-stop date and termination right.
8. **Repay Riverlark at Completion from price;** verify the funds flow deducts it.
9. **Treat bonuses (with on-costs) and unavoidable supplier commitments as debt-like items.**
10. **Make Ironquay payment and confirmatory assignment a CP;** add a broader IP ownership indemnity.
11. **Obtain a privacy forensic report** before signing; add a specific indemnity and a privacy warranty.
12. **Confirm lease and Mossvale consent requirements** and make them CPs or indemnities as appropriate.
13. **Run independent title searches** and require executed transfers.
14. **Require a bring-down** of the disclosure letter and data room from 22 September to signing, given the date gap.
15. **Obtain specialist input** from Australian privacy, tax and NSW limitation counsel to confirm the statutory points flagged above.
